headline: Sea Limited: revenue up 43% and Shopee orders up 26%, but heavier marketing and credit provisions cap profit; shares slide
takeaway: Revenue rose 43% to $8.6 billion and net income 34% to $502.5 million, or $0.92 a diluted share, about 6% below the $0.97 consensus. Shopee’s ad and commission revenue grew 51% and Monee’s loan book 60%, but marketing spend rose 64% and credit provisions 82%, and the shares fell 5% on the day.
results: Sea Limited reported revenue of $8.58 billion for the third quarter, up 43.4%, and gross profit of $3.94 billion, up 51.4%. Operating income rose 39.5% to $664 million and net income 34.0% to $502.5 million. Adjusted EBITDA rose 28.9% to $931 million. Diluted EPS was $0.9152 against $0.7612 a year earlier.

Shopee processed 4.5 billion orders, up 25.5%, on gross merchandise value of $39.7 billion, up 23.3%. Core marketplace revenue — commissions and advertising — rose 50.6% to $4.6 billion, while logistics-related revenue was flat at $724 million. Shopee’s adjusted EBITDA rose 44.7% to $269 million. Monee, the digital-finance arm, grew revenue 63.9% to $1.6 billion, with loans outstanding up 60% to $12.6 billion and 90-day non-performing loans at 1.3% against 1.1%; its adjusted EBITDA rose 15.5% to $298 million. Garena bookings rose 5.9% to $890 million and adjusted EBITDA 45.9% to $458 million.

Costs grew faster than revenue: sales and marketing rose 64% to $1.89 billion and provisions for credit losses 82% to $682 million, while research and development rose only 5%. Sea has completed its $1 billion buyback, repurchasing 11.1 million shares, and the board approved another $1 billion with no expiry.
mgmt: Chairman and chief executive Forrest Li said the momentum of the first half continued, with Shopee setting new records on both revenue and profit thanks to a growing buyer base, stronger monetisation and better unit economics. He said Monee is reaching more users and extending credit into more everyday spending, on and off Shopee, while staying disciplined on risk.

At Garena, Free Fire delivered strong bookings growth and Arena of Valor kept up the momentum from its tenth anniversary. Quarterly active users were steady at 672 million and paying users rose 4.1% to 68.6 million, a paying ratio of 10.2%.
view: Sea is three businesses with very different jobs. Garena is the cash cow, Free Fire still printing close to half a billion dollars of quarterly EBITDA; Shopee is the franchise, the dominant e-commerce platform in South-East Asia and growing in Brazil; and Monee is the profit engine that lends to Shopee’s buyers and sellers. This quarter showed all three working, but it also showed the trade-off management is making: it is choosing to reinvest heavily to defend and extend Shopee’s lead rather than let margins expand quickly.

The marketing line is the crux. A 64% increase in sales and marketing, while core marketplace revenue grows 51%, means Shopee is buying its growth — almost certainly in response to TikTok Shop in Indonesia and Thailand and to Mercado Libre and Temu in Brazil. Shopee’s EBITDA of $269 million on $39.7 billion of GMV is a margin of about 0.7%, well below the 1%-plus investors had hoped for by now. The rise in credit provisions is partly the mechanical cost of a loan book growing 60% under upfront-provisioning rules, but non-performing loans edging up from 1.1% to 1.3% deserves watching as the book extends off-platform.

The share price has fallen sharply this month and now sits at around 23 times trailing earnings, a much lower multiple than at any point in Sea’s growth phase. That price implies the market doubts Shopee can ever earn the margins of Alibaba or MercadoLibre in its region. The bull case is that Sea is deliberately under-earning, with take rates still rising and logistics costs falling, and that profits will step up once competition stabilises. The bear case is that South-East Asian e-commerce is permanently contested and the reinvestment never ends. This quarter gave evidence to both, which is why the shares fell.
watch: Watch Shopee’s adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of GMV, the trend in Monee’s non-performing loans as lending moves off-platform, Free Fire bookings into 2027, and how much of the new $1 billion buyback is used at current prices.
